title: Super El Niño! Why Is Singapore So Hot And Dry? | TheOneApp, Explored EP13
desc:
In November 2026, the end of the year, Singapore still felt like an oven. Why? Shrink down with Pip, Momo and Basil and BE a gust of the trade wind over the Pacific Ocean: push the warm water west, watch it evaporate and condense into rain clouds, then grow weaker and watch the warm water slide back east, taking the warm, wet air that builds the rain clouds with it. That is El Niño. Find out what makes this one a Super El Niño, name the water cycle (evaporation and condensation), see how a drier year made the haze worse here in Singapore, and what El Niño is doing to the weather in India and the USA. Then be a weather detective with two cups of water.

0:00 Why does it feel like an oven?
0:35 You are the trade wind
1:45 The headline
1:59 What makes it super
2:15 The water cycle
2:45 Here in Singapore: the haze
3:09 Meanwhile in India and the USA
3:42 Try this

Sources:
- NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion, 12 November 2026: a strong to very strong El Niño is likely through January to March 2027 (cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_advisory/ensodisc.shtml)
- Meteorological Service Singapore (NEA) news release, 29 May 2026: El Niño conditions expected in the second half of 2026, with warmer and drier weather from June to October (nea.gov.sg)
- National Environment Agency, Haze Situation Update, 9 October 2026: 24-hour PSI 135 to 192, Unhealthy (nea.gov.sg)
- India Meteorological Department, end of the 2026 south-west monsoon (30 September 2026): 759.4 mm against a normal of 868.6 mm, 12.6% below normal, the weakest since 2015 (as reported by Indian news)
- NOAA Climate Prediction Center, winter outlook update for December 2026 to February 2027 (19 November 2026): wetter than usual across the south, warmer than usual across the north (noaa.gov)
- How El Niño works: NOAA, Understanding El Niño (noaa.gov/understanding-el-nino)

title: Only 2 °C? How A Super El Niño Changes The World's Weather #Shorts
desc:
The middle of the Pacific is more than two degrees Celsius warmer than usual: a Super El Niño. Across a whole ocean, that is a huge amount of heat. This year India's monsoon brought about one-eighth less rain, and the USA expects a wetter south and a warmer north this winter. Watch the full episode: Super El Niño! Why Is Singapore So Hot And Dry? (TheOneApp, Explored EP13)

Sources: NOAA Climate Prediction Center (12 and 19 November 2026); India Meteorological Department (30 September 2026)
